title: Compute payable amounts in integer minor units, reductions before tax

facts.note: Bun conventions catalog; code may run on Node.
Tests are the evidence, not the subject.
Domain is where the calculation belongs; application/routes fire when money arithmetic appears there instead.
Task text mentions pricing, adjustments or tax.
Code computing a payable amount is written or changed.
Content observer: arithmetic (+ - * /, Math.round/floor/ceil, toFixed, parseFloat) on identifiers named like price/amount/total/discount/credit/tax/balance, or decimal literals in such expressions.
Whether reductions precede tax, rounding happens once per derived amount, and credits are consumed only up to the offset amount needs semantic judgement.

fires: A checkout/invoice function multiplies a decimal price by a tax rate and then subtracts a discount.
A use case applies a wallet or account-balance credit to an amount due and debits the full credit even when it exceeds the amount.
A route handler computes subtotal, discount and tax inline with floats and `toFixed(2)`.
A percentage voucher is converted to money and rounded at several intermediate steps.
doesNotFire: Displaying/formatting an already-computed integer amount for the UI.
Test files that assert on the calculation's outputs.
Passing an amount computed elsewhere through unchanged (persisting or forwarding it).

given: Code computes a payable amount from a base price, reductions (discounts, credits, stored value used as payment) and tax.
when: That calculation is written or changed.
then: Compute it in integer minor units, applying reductions before tax and taxing the reduced base, with exactly one explicit rounding step per derived amount.
prefer: One pure domain function with explicit inputs returning every part: `price({subtotal, discount, credit, taxBps}) => {subtotal, discount, creditUsed, taxable, tax, total}`.
Order: discount, then credit/stored value, then `tax = Math.round(taxable * taxBps / 10_000)` once.
Convert other units (%, stored-value units) to minor units once, with a named integer rounding rule.
Clamp at 0 and consume only what offsets: `creditUsed = Math.min(credit, remaining)`; the rest stays untouched.
avoid: Floats for money (`19.99`, `toFixed`, `* 1.2`) or re-rounding intermediate values.
Taxing the pre-reduction price; computing parts inside the route.
Negative totals; debiting or discarding a credit's unused excess.
unless: The domain explicitly defines another order (tax-inclusive prices, credit applied after tax): implement and document that order, still in integer minor units.
why: Float money and ad-hoc ordering yield off-by-a-cent totals, tax on money never charged and lost credit; one ordered integer computation is reproducible and testable.
evidence: Unit tests of the pure function cover boundaries: reduction equal to the base, reduction larger than the base (total 0, excess credit not consumed), rounding half cases for tax and percentage conversion, and zero inputs.
Tests assert every returned component (subtotal, each reduction, taxable, tax, total), proving the order, not only the total.
Reviewer sees no floating-point money arithmetic and exactly one rounding call per derived amount; the route only parses input, calls the function and serialises the result.
verifier_detail: Flag decimal literals, `parseFloat`, `toFixed`, or `/ 100` followed by further arithmetic on money-named identifiers in domain/application/routes source.
Flag more than one Math.round/floor/ceil on the same derived amount's data path, and rounding applied before the final step of a derived amount.
Flag tax computed from a value that has not had all reductions subtracted (unless a documented domain-specific order exists in code comments or docs).
Flag credit/stored-value consumption that uses the full credit rather than `min(credit, remaining)`, or totals that are not clamped at zero.
Flag money arithmetic spread across a route handler rather than a pure domain function with explicit rate/amount inputs.
Rates should be integers (e.g. hundredths of a percent, as in taxBps) or converted once; integer products must stay within Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (use bigint if amounts can exceed it).
audit: Written for PLT-85 as a new general convention from spec.md; no canonical source YAML.
Supporting knowledge (pure domain function, returning all components, clamping and partial consumption, boundary tests) placed in prefer/avoid/evidence as supporting moves of the single obligation.
